competencies: The learner appreciates the role of entrepreneurship through the application of entrepreneurial skills and building a unique personal brand for the benefit of self and society.
The learner analyses the political, economic, social, demographic, and global environment to undertake opportunities, and manage and sustain an enterprise for self and community benefit.
The learner scans the environment, generates ideas, and selects viable business opportunities for self and community benefit.
The learner follows the correct steps of preparing a business plan, and designs a workable business plan for the benefit of self and society.
The learner produces quality products by using appropriate inputs and technology to minimise production costs and satisfy customer needs in the community.
The learner demonstrates proficiency in marketing products to customers by conducting thorough market research and utilising effective promotional strategies to maintain competitiveness in business.

The learner identifies social challenges within the community and develops innovative, sustainable enterprises that address these challenges, contributing to community development and environmental conservation.
The learner appreciates the importance of engaging in family business and recognizing gender partnership in the operation of a business for self and community development.
The learner utilises insurance services to safeguard businesses against risks that may result in financial losses to ensure sustainability.
The learner applies knowledge of Capital Markets by exploiting capital-raising opportunities and undertaking investments for self and national development.
The learner applies human resource recruitment skills and motivation principles to enhance effective employee performance for the success of the enterprise.

The learner generates and interprets financial statements for the purpose of determining the profitability and financial position of an enterprise in order to make appropriate financial decisions for the benefit of self and the community.
The learner complies with tax laws and guidelines in Uganda to become tax compliant and contribute to community and national development.
The learner manages and sustains a business in a competitive environment.
values: Respect for humanity and the environment
Honesty, upholding and defending the truth at all times
Justice and fairness in dealing with others
Integrity; moral uprightness and sound character

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates the importance of engaging in family business and recognizing gender partnership in the operation of a business for self and community development.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: explore the role of small and medium enterprises; reasons for SMEs' high rate of failures in Uganda and solutions; and the need for sustainable growth. (u, gs, v)
examine the importance of family businesses; challenges associated with family businesses and solutions to overcome the challenges associated with family businesses in Uganda. (u, gs, v)
examine the factors that enhance gender partnership; barriers to women’s participation in entrepreneurship and solutions to the barriers to women’s participation in entrepreneurship. (u, gs, v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups learners: a) use the jig saw method on: i) concepts of small and medium enterprises. ii) role of small and medium enterprises in development. iii) reasons for SMEs' high rate of failures in Uganda and solutions. b) read a case study highlighting the best practices and strategies for the growth of small and medium enterprises. Let learners prepare and present the findings to the class.

In groups learners: a) Visit the nearby community and inquire about the following: i) Identify businesses run by family ii) importance of family businesses. iii) challenges associated with family businesses. iv) solutions to overcome challenges associated with family businesses. Task learners to prepare a report on their findings and make a presentation to the class.

In groups learners: a) use library resources and ICT gadgets to search and discuss the: i) Factors enhancing gender partnership. ii) Barriers to women’s participation in entrepreneurship. iii) Solutions to barriers to women’s participation in entrepreneurship. Guide learners to present their work to the class.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners’ presentations on the concepts and role of SMEs, reasons for their high rate of failure, and solutions to establish whether they; i) demonstrate active participation ii) suggest and develop new solutions iii) exhibit hard work for self-reliance
Converse with learners while asking probing questions to allow them to explore their critical thinking and problem-solving skills in small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Uganda.
Evaluate the learners’ presentations on small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Uganda and give feedback for improvement.

Observe learners visit the nearby community to collect information on family business to establish whether they: i) plan and carry out investigations ii) work effectively in diverse teams iii) evaluate different solutions iv) exhibit integrity, moral uprightness, and sound character
Converse with learners as they present their findings from the field while asking probing questions to establish their understanding of family business
Assess the learners’ reports on family business and make comments for improvement

Observe learners discuss gender partnership in business and take note of how they: i) read accurately and fluently ii) use ICT to search for information. iii) Appreciate culture diversity iv) Exhibit justice and fairness when dealing with others
Converse with learners while asking probing questions to establish their understanding of gender partnership in entrepreneurship.
Assess the learners’ presentation on gender partnership and make comments for improvement.

practicals.title: Field Study on Family Businesses
practicals.description_verbatim: Visit the nearby community and inquire about the following: i) Identify businesses run by family ii) importance of family businesses. iii) challenges associated with family businesses. iv) solutions to overcome challenges associated with family businesses.

suggested_uses: use library resources and ICT gadgets to search and discuss

topics.core_competency: The learner utilises insurance services to safeguard businesses against risks that may result in financial losses to ensure sustainability.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine the concept of insurance including meaning; common terms used; types and classes of insurance and principles governing the operation of insurance in the community. (k, u, gs, v)

analyse the importance of insurance; insurance documentation; steps followed when processing an insurance contract/policy; challenges faced by the insurance business and the solutions for sustainability. (k, s, g)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups learners: a) use library resources and ICT gadgets to search about insurance and discuss the: i) meaning of insurance ii) common terms used in insurance iii) types and classes of insurance iv) principles of insurance Let learners share the findings with the class.

In groups learners: a) use library resources and ICT gadgets to search the: i) importance of insurance ii) insurance documentation iii) steps followed when processing an insurance contract. iv) challenges facing the insurance industry in Uganda v) solutions to the challenges. Task learners to write and present a report about their findings to the class.

a) Listen to the presentation of an insurance expert on: i) the importance of insurance to the business community ii) principles and policies of insurance iii) challenges faced by the insurance industry and solutions to the challenges. b) Take note of the above key aspects from the presentation of the insurance expert Guide them to write and present a report to the class from the guest speakers’ presentation.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they search and discuss about insurance and take note of how they: i) talk confidently and explain ideas clearly. ii) listen attentively to one another iii) exhibit honesty, and uphold and defend the truth at all times.
Converse with the learners to evaluate their understanding of insurance concepts.
Assess the learners’ output during the brainstorming session to critique their responses.

Observe the learners as they search and discuss and take note of how they: i) use ICT to search for information. ii) talk confidently and explain opinions clearly. iii) Write and present their reports coherently
Converse with learners and explore the extent to which they recognize insurance documentation, contract, importance, challenges, and solutions.
Evaluate the learners’ reports on insurance in business and give comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they interact with the insurance expert and assess their: i) ability to attentively listen to the Guest Speaker. ii) ability to use logical reasoning when asking relevant questions to the guest speaker iii) ability to write reports and present them coherently to the class
Converse with learners to assess their conceptualisation of insurance in business.
Evaluate the learners’ reports on insurance in Uganda and make comments for improvement

suggested_uses: use library resources and ICT gadgets to search about insurance

topics.core_competency: The learner applies knowledge of Capital Markets by exploiting capital-raising opportunities and undertaking investments for self and national development.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine the role of Capital Markets: terms used; key players; and their laws and regulations in the economic development of Uganda. (k, u, gs)
explore the process followed to access investment products in capital markets, utilise them for the benefit of self and society. (k, u, gs)

utilise the different business financing opportunities in Uganda’s securities exchange, process and benefits of listing a company and capital raising options for business growth within the Capital Markets of Uganda. (k, u, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups learners: a) read textbook extracts on capital markets and/or navigate the Capital Markets Authority Website (www.cmauganda.co.ug), to search and discuss: i) the concept of capital markets. ii) terms used in capital markets. iii) key players in capital markets. iv) laws and regulations governing capital markets in Uganda. v) the role of Capital Markets and Capital Markets Authority (CMA). in the Financial Sector. Task learners to write a report on the findings and present it to the class for peer critiquing.

In groups learners: a) use textbook extracts on capital markets in Uganda to search and discuss: i) investment products in capital markets of Uganda. ii) benefits of engaging in investment products. iii) Process followed to access investment products in Capital Markets. Let learners display their work in class for a gallery walk and peer critiquing.

In groups learners: a) read a case study on financing opportunities for issuers in capital markets and discuss: i) examples of issuers of financing opportunities in private and public companies. ii) the process and benefits of listing a company on a Ugandan securities exchange. iii) capital raising options for businesses which include: • Government bonds • Corporate bonds • Sale of private/public equity Make learners share their findings with the class.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they search and discuss terms used; key players; their laws and regulations and their role in the economic development of Uganda. ascertain whether they; i) use ICT to search on capital markets. ii) work collaboratively in teams to generate ideas on capital markets.
Converse with learners by probing them on capital markets to establish their critical thinking skills.
Evaluate the learners’ report on capital markets in Uganda and give feedback for improvement.

Observe the learners as they search and discuss investment products, benefits of engaging in investment products and process followed to access investment products. Assess how they: i) read accurately and fluently. ii) develop ideas by considering different perspectives on investment products in capital markets. iii) exhibit hard work for self-reliance
Converse with learners to assess their conceptualisation of investment products in capital markets by asking them probing questions.
Assess the learners’ output on investment products in capital markets in Uganda and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they read and discuss financing opportunities for issuers in capital markets and take note of their ability to: i) use logical reasoning. ii) speak confidently and explain ideas clearly. iii) work independently with persistence. iv) exhibit honesty, and uphold and defend the truth at all times.
Engage learners in a dialogue while asking probing questions to assess their level of understanding of financing opportunities for issuers in capital markets.
Assess the learners’ output from the case study and make comments for improvement.

suggested_uses: navigate the Capital Markets Authority Website (www.cmauganda.co.ug)
use ICT to search on capital markets

themes.theme_title: TOPIC 11: Human Resources in an Enterprise

topics.core_competency: The learner applies human resource recruitment skills and motivation principles to enhance effective employee performance for the success of the enterprise.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: explore the labour requirements and procedures followed when recruiting employees for an enterprise to increase productivity. (s, gs, v)
evaluate the effectiveness of motivation strategies and remuneration for enhancing employee performance in an enterprise. (k, u, gs, v)
design strategies for managing labour turnover in an enterprise. (u, s, gs v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups learners: a) use text materials on human resource management or ICT gadgets to search and discuss the: i) meaning of human resource management ii) elements of human resource management Make learners present their work to the class for peer critiquing.

b) use textbook extracts on human resource management to search and discuss the: i) factors considered when deciding on the type and number of employees. ii) sources of recruiting employees. iii) procedures of recruiting employees in an enterprise. Guide learners to write an essay about their findings and present it to the class

In groups learners: a) Use guided discovery to explore and discuss the: i) methods of paying workers and factors that determine workers’ payments in an enterprise. ii) employee motivation strategies in an enterprise. Task learners to present their work to the class for further guidance.

a) Read a case study on employee training for a selected enterprise in Uganda and discuss the: i) Meaning of training ii) Rationale for training employees in an enterprise iii) Process of training employees in an enterprise iv) Employee Training methods in an enterprise Make learners write an essay on their findings and present it to the class

In groups learners: a) Conduct a field study in the nearby business community to establish the possible causes of labour turnover, its costs to the business and strategies for reducing it. Guide learners to write a report on their findings and present it to the class.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe the learners as they search and discuss the meaning and elements of human resource management and take note of their ability to: i) use ICT to create, manipulate and process information. ii) take responsibility for their learning. iii) talk confidently and explain ideas clearly. iv) exhibit respect for one another.
Converse with the learners by asking probing questions to establish their understanding and maturity in reasoning as they discuss the meaning and elements of human resource management.
Assess the learners’ write up on the meaning and elements of human resource management and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners discuss the factors considered when deciding the type and number of employees, sources of recruitment and procedures of recruitment to assess their ability to: i) Use ICT to search for information. ii) exhibit honesty, and uphold and defend the truth all the time.

Converse with learners while asking probing questions to evaluate their understanding of the factors considered when deciding the type and number of employees, sources of recruitment and procedures of recruiting labour in an enterprise.
Assess learners’ output on factors considered when deciding the type and number of employees, sources of recruitment and procedures of recruiting labour and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they discuss the employee motivation strategies and workers’ payments in an enterprise to ascertain whether they: i) work with others collaboratively. ii) take responsibility for their learning. iii) exhibit integrity, moral uprightness and sound character.
Converse with learners to assess their conceptualization of employee motivation strategies and remuneration in an enterprise.
Assess the learners’ presentation on employee motivation strategies and remuneration in an enterprise, give comments for improvements.
Observe the learners as they read the case study on employee training discuss and present, and take note of how they: i) read accurately and fluently. ii) Suggest and develop new solutions.
Converse with learners while asking probing questions to establish their conceptualization of employee training in an enterprise.
Evaluate learners’ essays on employee training in an enterprise and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they interact with the business community to establish causes of labour turnover and its costs to the business while taking note of their ability to: i) Interact effectively with others ii) talk confidently and explain ideas clearly iii) respect for humanity and the environment
Converse with the learners and assess their understanding on the causes, costs of labour turnover in an enterprise and strategies of managing it.
Evaluate the learners’ field reports on the causes, costs of labour turnover in business and strategies of managing it. Give feedback for improvement.

practicals.title: Field Study on Labour Turnover
practicals.description_verbatim: Conduct a field study in the nearby business community to establish the possible causes of labour turnover, its costs to the business and strategies for reducing it.

suggested_uses: use text materials on human resource management or ICT gadgets to search and discuss
Use ICT to search for information

topics.core_competency: The learner generates and interprets financial statements for the purpose of determining the profitability and financial position of an enterprise in order to make appropriate financial decisions for the benefit of self and the community.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: estimate the financial requirements for a selected business and effectively manage the flow of funds in an enterprise. (u, gs, v)
prepare and interpret financial statements in an enterprise. (s, gs, v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups learners: a) brainstorm and discuss the financial requirements for an enterprise Task them to share their findings with the class.

a) Use textbook extracts on financial management in the business, search and discuss the controls used to manage the inflow and outflow of funds in an enterprise. b) Read a case study containing cash inflows and outflows of a given business and prepare the cash flow statement. Guide them to make a presentation of their work to the class.

In groups learners: a) study the financial records of their school business club or a selected business to prepare financial statements and determine: i) the profitability of the business. ii) the financial position of the business. Task them to display their statements in class for a gallery walk and peer critiquing.

In groups learners: a) Study the financial statements of a given enterprise to compute and interpret the; i) Profitability Ratios ii) Efficiency Ratios iii) Liquidity Ratios iv) Solvency Ratios Make them display their work for peer critiquing in a gallery walk.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners brainstorm and discuss the financial requirements to assess how they: i) talk confidently and explain ideas clearly. ii) work independently with persistence. iii) exhibit honesty, and uphold and defend the truth at all times.
Converse with the learners to evaluate their understanding of the financial requirements needed to start a selected enterprise
Assess the learners’ output during the brainstorming session, and critique their responses for improvement.

Observe the learners as they research and discuss the controls used to manage the inflow and outflow of funds in a business and take note of how they: i) talk confidently and explain ideas clearly. ii) predict outcomes and make reasoned decisions. iii) exhibit honesty, and uphold and defend the truth at all times.
In a conversation with the learners establish their understanding and reasoning on the controls used to manage the inflow and outflow of funds in a business.
Evaluate the learners write up on the controls used to manage the inflow and outflow of funds in a business.

Observe the learners prepare financial statements for their school business club or a selected business, and ascertain whether they: i) use inductive and deductive logic. ii) use numbers and measurements accurately. iii) exhibit integrity, moral uprightness and sound character
Converse with the learners while asking probing questions to establish their conceptualisation of financial statements in a business to encourage critical thinking skills.
Evaluate the learners’ output on financial statements in an enterprise and make comments for improvement.

Observe the learners’ computation skills as they analyse, calculate and interpret financial statements using ratios of an enterprise, take note of their ability to: i) use numbers and measurements accurately. ii) analyse mathematical data to make predictions and justify decisions. iii) work out and solve mathematical problems. iv) exhibit integrity, moral uprightness and sound character when dealing with mathematical data.

Converse with the learners by asking probing questions to establish their accuracy in analysing and interpreting financial ratios, establish whether they have the: i) correct formulae. ii) correct substitutions. iii) correct ratios. iv) correct interpretations.
Evaluate the learners’ output on the interpretation of financial statements of an enterprise and give feedback for improvement.

topics.core_competency: The learner complies with tax laws and guidelines in Uganda to become tax compliant and contribute to community and national development.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: examine the role of taxation in the economic development of the country. (k, s, gs, v)
comply with tax laws including factors influencing and factors limiting tax compliance in a country with reference to Uganda. (u, s, gs, v).
demonstrate computation of different taxes paid in Uganda. (u, s, gs, v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups Learners; a) brainstorm the meaning of taxation and terminologies used in taxation. b) Participate in a debating session on the role of taxation in the economic development of Uganda.
a) Use URA text materials or web portal or ICT devices to search and discuss the: i) principles/canons of a good tax system. ii) types of taxes. Let learners present their work to the class.

In groups Learners; a) visit URA web portal or text materials to search and discuss the following: i) The concept and elements of tax compliance ii) Factors influencing tax compliance iii) Factors limiting tax compliance in Uganda Select group representatives to present the findings to the class for peer critiquing.

a) Use URA text materials/web portal or ICT devices to search and discuss the: i) forms and effects of non-tax compliance. ii) benefits of tax compliance. iii) strategies for improving tax compliance in Uganda. Make them present their work to the class for peer critiquing

In groups learners; a) use text materials or URA manuals on tax computations, discuss and calculate the following domestic taxes: i) Corporation Tax ii) Individual Income Tax iii) Employment Income Tax (PAYE) iv) Presumptive Tax v) Rental Income Tax vi) Withholding Tax vii) Value Added Tax (VAT) Let learners demonstrate their work to the class for peer critiquing.

b) Use text materials or URA manuals on tax computations, discuss and calculate the following international trade taxes: i) Import Tax ii) Excise Duty iii) Value Added Tax (VAT) iv) Withholding Tax v) Environmental levy vi) Infrastructure Levy Make learners demonstrate their work to the class for peer critiquing.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners brainstorm the meaning of taxation and terminologies used in taxation and debate on the role of taxation in the economic development of Uganda. Assess their ability to: i) talk confidently and explain ideas clearly. ii) exhibit honesty, uphold and defend the truth at all times
Converse with the learners to establish their accuracy in responding to the concept of taxation and terminologies used in taxation.
Evaluate the learners’ output during the debating session on taxation. Critique their responses for improvement.

Observe the learners as they search and discuss the canons of taxation, and types of taxes and take note of whether they: i) use ICT to create, manipulate and process information. ii) take responsibility for their learning.
Converse with the learners to establish their understanding and maturity in reasoning on the canons of taxation, types of taxes
Evaluate the learners’ write-up on taxation and make comments for improvement.

Observe the learners as they search and discuss the concept of tax compliance, factors influencing and limiting tax compliance and take note of their ability to: i) use ICT to collaborate, communicate and refine work. ii) talk confidently and explain opinions clearly. iii) show respect for one another. iv) write and present their work coherently.
Converse with the learners to establish their understanding and maturity in reasoning as they discuss the concept of tax compliance, factors influencing and limiting tax compliance.
Evaluate the learners’ presentations on the concept of tax compliance, factors influencing and limiting tax compliance and make comments for improvement.

Observe learners as they search and discuss the forms, benefits and ways of improving tax compliance establish whether they: i) exhibit active participation. ii) work collaboratively in diverse teams. iii) exhibit honesty, and uphold and defend the truth at all times.
Converse with the learners to establish their understanding of the forms, effects, benefits and strategies of improving tax compliance in Uganda.
evaluate the learners’ presentations on the forms, effects, benefits and ways of improving tax compliance in Uganda, make comments for improvement.

Observe the learners as they calculate different taxes and establish whether they: i) use numbers and tax rates accurately. ii) use mathematics to justify and support decisions. iii) exhibit integrity and honesty on taxes.

Converse with the learners by asking probing questions to establish their accuracy in calculating taxes, and establish whether they have the: i) correct formulae ii) correct substitution iii) correct answers
Evaluate the learners’ output on tax computations and give feedback for improvement.

Observe the learners calculate different taxes to ascertain whether they: i) use numbers and tax rates accurately. ii) use mathematics to justify and support decisions iii) interpret and interrogate mathematical data correctly iv) exhibit integrity, moral uprightness and sound character

Converse with the learners by asking probing questions to establish their accuracy in calculating taxes, and establish whether they have the: i) Correct formulae ii) Correct Substitution iii) Correct answers
Evaluate the learners’ output on tax computations and give feedback for improvement.

suggested_uses: Use URA text materials or web portal or ICT devices to search and discuss

topics.core_competency: The learner manages and sustains a business in a competitive environment.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: evaluate and manage business competition in an enterprise. (u, gs, v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups learners: a) Use Think-Pair-Share to discuss the: i) meaning of business competition. ii) types of competition in business. Let learners share their findings with the class for peer critiquing.

b) Read textbook extracts on business competition and discuss: i) factors a business should consider when analysing business competition. ii) ways of maintaining a competitive advantage in business. iii) effects of competition in business. Make learners present their work to the plenary.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss and critique each other on the meaning of business competition and its types, and establish whether they: i) talk confidently and explain ideas clearly ii) respect one another
Converse with learners while asking probing questions to evaluate their understanding of the meaning of business competition and its types.
Assess the learners’ output on the meaning of business competition and its types and make comments for improvement.
Observe learners as they discuss business competition and establish whether they: i) work with others to generate ideas ii) read accurately and fluently

Converse with learners while asking probing questions to establish their understanding of the: i) factors a business should consider when analysing business competition. ii) ways of maintaining a competitive advantage in business. iii) effects of competition in business.
Evaluate the learners’ output on business competition and give feedback for improvement.
